name: @sarutobi-sasuke/lmms-mcp

tools.name: list_external_tools
tools.description: Discover optional renderer dependencies, VST3 instruments and upstream setup links.

tools.name: render_vst3_stems
tools.description: Render named tracks from an editable format 1 MIDI export with configured VST3 instruments, up to 10 minutes, with an optional reverb per track. Return aligned stereo WAVs, a mix and a reproducible assignment manifest. Leave a few seconds after the last note for the release and reverb tail.

dspreset.description: A Decent Sampler preset in the workspace, for example from convert_sfz. Use instead of preset; instrument must be decent-sampler.

width.description: Stereo width of the instrument before the reverb: 0 is mono, 1 unchanged. Wide sampled pianos often need 0.5 to 0.7 to hold together in mono.

eq.description: EQ after the instrument, before the reverb. For example a highshelf at 3500 Hz +3 dB to brighten a soft piano.

reverb.description: Add a room to this track after the instrument, for example { wet: 0.22, roomSize: 0.75 } for a piano in a hall. The stem keeps its reverb, so the stems still sum to the mix.

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Read the LMMS MCP workflow and discover the local setup before composing, editing or exporting.

tools.name: list_composer_profiles
tools.description: Find composer studies by name, musical technique or game use.

tools.name: create_composer_sketch
tools.description: Write an original editable LMMS sketch based on a composer profile. Uses stock instruments and suggests a Fathom patch for the motif.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create an editable 4/4 LMMS project. One bar is 192 ticks, one beat is 48. Each pattern takes raw notes, a drum step grid, a melody line or a chord progression. Stock drum notes play at original pitch on MIDI 69; give one-shots a note length that covers the sample. The song is pinned to lengthBars (default: the last declared pattern bar) even when its final bars are empty.

voice.description: pluck, bass and pad are built-in synths; kick, clap and hat are stock one-shots; sample plays a workspace WAV or a stock LMMS sample; preset loads a factory preset.

factorySample.description: Stock LMMS sample such as "drums/snare01.ogg". See list_samples.

role.description: What the track is for. Use one lead at a time and at most one counter-melody.

notes.description: Raw notes. tick and length are in ticks from the pattern start (48 per beat).

steps.description: Drum grid, tiled to fill the pattern: X accent, x hit, o soft, g ghost, - rest. Example "x---o---x-x-o---". Default 16 steps per bar, 48-tick notes at MIDI 69.

melody.description: Melody line of NOTE:steps[:velocity] tokens, r:steps for rests, [D4,F4,A4]:8 for chords, | ignored. Example "D5:3 F5:3 A5:6 G5:2 F5:2". Repeats to fill the pattern.

chords.description: Chord progression such as "Dm Bb F C" (one bar each; "Dm:2" lasts two bars), looped to fill the pattern. style: block, pulse, arp (order, rate in steps) or bass (figure).

tuning.description: How preset voices are tuned; see apply_preset.

strict.description: Stop with an error, writing nothing, when an arrangement check reports an error.

tools.name: inspect_project
tools.description: Read saved instrument tracks, pattern locations and note counts.

tools.name: read_pattern
tools.description: Read the notes in a saved instrument pattern. Bar numbers start at zero.

tools.name: render_fathom_track
tools.description: Render LMMS piano-roll notes through Fathom Atelier’s synth worklet with cutoff automation. Save a WAV and an LMMS copy with the rendered audio and editable source notes.

tools.name: replace_pattern
tools.description: Replace one arrangement pattern, identified by track and bar. Writes a new project copy.

notes.description: Raw notes. tick and length are in ticks from the pattern start (48 per beat).

steps.description: Drum grid, tiled to fill the pattern: X accent, x hit, o soft, g ghost, - rest. Example "x---o---x-x-o---". Default 16 steps per bar, 48-tick notes at MIDI 69.

melody.description: Melody line of NOTE:steps[:velocity] tokens, r:steps for rests, [D4,F4,A4]:8 for chords, | ignored. Example "D5:3 F5:3 A5:6 G5:2 F5:2". Repeats to fill the pattern.

chords.description: Chord progression such as "Dm Bb F C" (one bar each; "Dm:2" lasts two bars), looped to fill the pattern. style: block, pulse, arp (order, rate in steps) or bass (figure).

tools.name: add_pattern
tools.description: Add a pattern to an existing instrument track at an unused bar. Writes a new project copy.

notes.description: Raw notes. tick and length are in ticks from the pattern start (48 per beat).

steps.description: Drum grid, tiled to fill the pattern: X accent, x hit, o soft, g ghost, - rest. Example "x---o---x-x-o---". Default 16 steps per bar, 48-tick notes at MIDI 69.

melody.description: Melody line of NOTE:steps[:velocity] tokens, r:steps for rests, [D4,F4,A4]:8 for chords, | ignored. Example "D5:3 F5:3 A5:6 G5:2 F5:2". Repeats to fill the pattern.

chords.description: Chord progression such as "Dm Bb F C" (one bar each; "Dm:2" lasts two bars), looped to fill the pattern. style: block, pulse, arp (order, rate in steps) or bass (figure).

tools.name: add_track
tools.description: Add an instrument track with its patterns to an existing project. Writes a new project copy.

voice.description: pluck, bass and pad are built-in synths; kick, clap and hat are stock one-shots; sample plays a workspace WAV or a stock LMMS sample; preset loads a factory preset.

factorySample.description: Stock LMMS sample such as "drums/snare01.ogg". See list_samples.

role.description: What the track is for. Use one lead at a time and at most one counter-melody.

notes.description: Raw notes. tick and length are in ticks from the pattern start (48 per beat).

steps.description: Drum grid, tiled to fill the pattern: X accent, x hit, o soft, g ghost, - rest. Example "x---o---x-x-o---". Default 16 steps per bar, 48-tick notes at MIDI 69.

melody.description: Melody line of NOTE:steps[:velocity] tokens, r:steps for rests, [D4,F4,A4]:8 for chords, | ignored. Example "D5:3 F5:3 A5:6 G5:2 F5:2". Repeats to fill the pattern.

chords.description: Chord progression such as "Dm Bb F C" (one bar each; "Dm:2" lasts two bars), looped to fill the pattern. style: block, pulse, arp (order, rate in steps) or bass (figure).

strict.description: Stop with an error, writing nothing, when an arrangement check reports an error.

tools.name: remove_track
tools.description: Remove an instrument track and any automation clips linked to it. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: copy_bars
tools.description: Repeat a section: copy every pattern that lies inside a bar range to a new position, on all instrument tracks or the named ones. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: set_song_length
tools.description: Pin the song to an exact number of bars so loops keep empty closing bars, or pass null to remove the pin. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: save_project_copy
tools.description: Copy a native saved project between .mmp and .mmpz, preserving its XML content.

tools.name: set_track_mix
tools.description: Change volume (0-200, fractions allowed), pan, mute or solo on one instrument track. Solo is honoured by render_mix. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: set_master
tools.description: Set master volume (0-200) and master pitch in semitones. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: list_presets
tools.description: List installed factory presets: native .xpf paths, plus ZynAddSubFX bank folders with counts (pass a bank to list its .xiz patches).

tools.name: render_mix
tools.description: Render the song to a 48 kHz WAV or OGG and report duration, peak, RMS, loudness, clipped samples and the loop boundary jump. Honours solo. Optional loop-safe tail and loudness mastering.

tail.description: cut: stop at the last bar (default). wrap: fold the reverb and delay tail back onto the start for a seamless loop. keep: let the tail ring out (one extra bar).

targetLufs.description: Integrated loudness target in LUFS, for example -16 for game music.

ceilingDb.description: Peak ceiling in dBFS for the built-in limiter (default -1 when a loudness target is set).

tools.name: render_stems
tools.description: Render one WAV per instrument, sample or Beat/Bassline track, all aligned to the mix length. Works for full-length songs; renders run in parallel.

tracks.description: Only these track names (default: every unmuted audio track).

tools.name: analyze_audio
tools.description: Measure a workspace WAV so you can judge a mix without hearing it: integrated loudness (LUFS), true peak, RMS, crest, clipping, DC, stereo correlation, energy in six frequency bands, spectral centroid, loop seam, optional per-section levels and pitch, plus plain-language warnings. Can return a spectrogram image.

bpm.description: Needed when sections are given in bars.

loop.description: Check the file as a loop.

targetLufs.description: Integrated loudness target in LUFS, for example -16 for game music.

spectrogram.description: Also write this PNG to the workspace and return it as an image.

tools.name: list_samples
tools.description: Browse the stock LMMS sample library (drums, basses, instruments, strings, effects and more). Returns factorySample paths for sample tracks.

tools.name: apply_preset
tools.description: Load a factory preset (.xpf or ZynAddSubFX .xiz) onto a track. With the default concert tuning, presets saved at another base note are corrected so written notes sound at pitch; the result reports the measured offset and level. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: search_sounds
tools.description: Find sounds by name, role and character across factory presets, ZynAddSubFX patches and Fathom patches. Measured entries carry level, tuning, envelope and brightness tags.

tools.name: build_sound_catalogue
tools.description: Measure factory presets by rendering a test note, so search_sounds can filter by role, loudness, tuning and brightness. Processes up to `limit` unmeasured presets per call; call again until remaining is 0.

tools.name: preview_sound
tools.description: Render a short audition of a factory preset, stock sample or Fathom patch to a workspace WAV and report its level and detected pitch.

tools.name: list_instruments
tools.description: Discover what this installation can play: built-in voices, stock instrument plugins, preset and sample counts, effects, OGG support and Fathom bridge configuration.

tools.name: set_native_instrument
tools.description: Load an installed stock LMMS instrument at its default settings. Keeps existing notes, mixer routing and track controls. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: route_mixer_bus
tools.description: Create a mixer bus sending to Master and route named instrument tracks to it, for shared effects or group level. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: set_bus
tools.description: Set the gain (0-2, 1 is unity) or mute of a mixer channel, including Master. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: list_effects
tools.description: List the effects edit_effect can add, with every parameter, its range and default.

tools.name: inspect_effects
tools.description: Read the effect chain of an instrument track or mixer channel, including stored parameters.

tools.name: edit_effect
tools.description: Add, update or remove an effect on an instrument track or a mixer channel such as Master. Plugins: delay (tempo-synced, with feedback), reverb, compressor, limiter, amplifier, bassbooster, stereo, eq, crossovereq. See list_effects for parameters. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: automate_track
tools.description: Write an editable automation clip for an instrument track control: volume, pan, pitch (cents), filter cutoff (Hz) or resonance. A control can carry several clips at different positions. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: inspect_arrangement
tools.description: Read tempo, metre, song length, master volume, mixer routes, track levels, instrument types and timeline clips.

tools.name: set_project_tempo
tools.description: Set a static tempo. Existing note and clip ticks stay fixed. Tempo-synced delays keep their old time until updated. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: export_one_shots
tools.description: Trim edge silence, fade and peak-match source WAVs as mono 48 kHz game sound effects.

tools.name: edit_clip
tools.description: Move, duplicate, rename or remove an instrument pattern. Positions are absolute LMMS ticks. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: edit_sample_clip
tools.description: Place, move, duplicate, resize, mute, relink or remove a native sample clip. Positions and lengths use LMMS ticks. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: set_track_role
tools.description: Declare what an instrument track is for: drums, bass, harmony, lead, counter, texture or fx. Pass null to clear it. Writes a new project copy.

tools.name: lint_arrangement
tools.description: Check the arrangement of a saved project from its notes, with no rendering: role limits (one lead, at most one counter), competing melodies, register overlaps, harsh clashes on strong beats, out-of-key notes, crowded, empty or static bars, motif repetition and lead playability. Returns findings with a rule id, severity (error, warning, note), the bars (from zero) and tracks involved, and a one-sentence fix. Run it before rendering and fix every error before export.

key.description: Key such as "D minor", "Dm" or "A dorian". Detected from the notes when omitted.

tools.name: quality_report
tools.description: Score a project from 0 to 100 with the reasons listed, combining lint_arrangement findings with audio analysis of an optional rendered WAV (loudness, peaks, clipping, balance and loop seam). Fails on any arrangement error or a score under the threshold.

audio.description: A render of this project, for example from render_mix.

key.description: Key such as "D minor", "Dm" or "A dorian". Detected from the notes when omitted.

loop.description: Check the audio as a loop.

targetLufs.description: Integrated loudness target in LUFS, for example -16 for game music.

tools.name: build_audition_page
tools.description: Write a self-contained HTML page so a person can listen to and judge the music in seconds. Give either an export_game_audio folder (plays the intro into the loop gaplessly, with layer faders, mute and solo, stinger buttons and section jumps) or one to four workspace WAV or OGG files (played in sync and switched A/B at matched loudness). The listener rates sections and pins notes to the time, bar and layer state, then saves or copies feedback JSON for read_feedback. No network access; audio is referenced by relative path.

folder.description: Folder written by export_game_audio. The page is written into it.

manifest.description: Manifest in the folder. Needed only when the folder holds more than one.

files.description: Workspace WAV or OGG renders to compare, optionally one folder down. The page is written to the workspace root.

sections.description: Named sections in song bars counted from zero (the intro starts at bar 0). Lengths default to the next section.

bpm.description: Tempo for bar display and sections when comparing files. A game folder uses its manifest tempo.

spectrogram.description: Workspace PNG, for example from analyze_audio, shown under the player.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing page of the same name.

tools.name: read_feedback
tools.description: Read listener feedback saved or copied from an audition page and return it grouped by section and bar, with ratings, the weakest section and what the listener was hearing (layers muted or soloed, A/B file) for each note. Pass a workspace JSON file or the pasted text.

file.description: Feedback JSON in the workspace, optionally one folder down.

text.description: Feedback JSON pasted from the page's Copy feedback button.

tools.name: remember_taste
tools.description: Store a lasting listener preference in .lmms-taste.json in the workspace, for example "leads too busy, keep melodies sparse" or "less reverb on drums". Later sessions read it with get_taste. Repeated wording is stored once. Pass forget with entry ids to remove preferences that no longer hold. Pass repair: true to recover from a damaged file: the original is kept as a backup and the valid entries are kept.

area.description: What the preference is about: a track role, the mix, the arrangement, sound choice or general.

source.description: Where it came from, for example a feedback file name.

repair.description: Back up a damaged .lmms-taste.json and keep only its valid entries.

tools.name: get_taste
tools.description: Read the listener's stored preferences from .lmms-taste.json, grouped by area. Call this before composing or mixing. Pass area to get that area and the general entries.

tools.name: auto_balance
tools.description: Balance a mix by measurement in one call. Renders one stem per audio track, measures each over the loudest stretch of the song (or measureBars), decides each track's role (declared mcp-role, else a reported guess), sets track volumes so drums hit peak targets and pitched parts hit RMS targets over the time they sound, predicts the summed mix and lowers the master if the predicted peak would break the headroom. Scales volume automation instead of failing. If a track cannot reach its target, all targets come down together to keep the balance. Returns a per-track table, the predicted mix peak and loudness, a masking report and mono warnings. Refuses while any track is soloed. Targets are starting points, stated as stem levels at master volume 100; override them per role, drum kind or track.

output.description: Where to write the balanced project. Required unless dryRun.

dryRun.description: Measure and plan without writing a project.

measureBars.description: Bars to measure (zero-based). Default: the loudest 8 bars of the mix.

roles.description: By role (bass, lead, counter, harmony, texture, fx, drums) or drum kind (kick, snare, clap, hat, crash, tom, perc). Numbers use the role's own measure.

headroomDb.description: Keep the predicted mix peak this far under full scale.

master.description: protect: lower the master only when the predicted peak breaks the headroom (default). fit: set the master so the peak lands exactly on the headroom. keep: never touch it.

tools.name: compare_to_reference
tools.description: Measure how a render differs from a reference track: integrated loudness, band balance (each band relative to the file's own total, so overall level does not swamp it), crest factor, stereo correlation and spectral centroid, with the largest differences turned into plain suggestions. Optional sections compare matching passages; reference times default to the same as the audio.

tools.name: list_blueprints
tools.description: List tested plans for kinds of game music: overworld, battle, boss, calm town, dungeon tension, title or menu, puzzle or chill, chiptune, and a victory fanfare stinger. Each gives sections with bar counts and energy, which roles play where, register lanes, drum grids, bass figure, harmony style, where the lead states, varies and rests, starting sounds and catalogue alternatives.

tools.name: create_from_blueprint
tools.description: Write a full editable project from a blueprint. Give a key, bpm and a target length in seconds or bars (the nearest whole form is used and the exact duration reported), and ideally your own motif and chord progression so the music is original. The lead is built from the motif: stated, repeated, varied and rested. Every track gets a role, one lead and at most one counter sound at a time, support parts stay under the lead, and the song length is pinned. Returns the section map (name, start bar, bars) for replace_pattern, apply_edits and analyze_audio.

key.description: Such as "E minor", "F# dorian" or just "G" (keeps the blueprint mode). Default: the blueprint key.

motif.description: Your motif as a melody line, "D5:2 F5:2 A5:4 r:4", or scale degrees, "1:2 3:2 5:4 r:4". Any octave: it is moved into the lead lane. Keep it to one or two bars.

progression.description: Main progression as chord symbols ("Em C G D") or Roman numerals ("i VI III VII"). ":2" holds a chord two bars.

contrastProgression.description: Progression for the contrasting sections. Default: the blueprint one in your key.

sounds.description: default uses the blueprint voices; suggested swaps pitched tracks for the best measured factory preset for each role.

tools.name: compose_piece
tools.description: Write a complete arranged piece from a style and a seed in one call: chord progression, phrase-based melody, accompaniment, bass and drums, with an intro and an ending, saved as an editable project. Plain seeded code, so the same seed gives the same piece. Render it with render_mix, or use compose_batch to try many seeds.

style.description: chiptune: Bright 8-bit style tune with a square lead, fast arpeggios and a tight beat. adventure: Open, hopeful overworld theme with a singing lead over rolling chords. battle: Driving minor-key action cue with a busy lead and octave bass. ballad: Slow, gentle piece: a simple tune over held arpeggios with a light beat. swing: Easy swing: a laid-back tune, walking bass and a ride pattern.

key.description: Such as "D minor". Default: chosen from the style by the seed.

voices.description: Replace the sound of any part, for example {"lead": {"voice": "preset", "preset": "TripleOscillator/Square.xpf", "volume": 14}}.

tools.name: compose_batch
tools.description: Compose several seeds of the same recipe, render each one, and rank them by measured checks: the arrangement lint, mix warnings from the render, and a tune score (stepwise motion, range, breathing room, rhythmic variety, one clear peak). Returns the ranking with reasons so a listener only needs to hear the top few. The scores catch faults; they cannot tell whether a tune is good.

targetLufs.description: Integrated loudness target in LUFS, for example -16 for game music.

style.description: chiptune: Bright 8-bit style tune with a square lead, fast arpeggios and a tight beat. adventure: Open, hopeful overworld theme with a singing lead over rolling chords. battle: Driving minor-key action cue with a busy lead and octave bass. ballad: Slow, gentle piece: a simple tune over held arpeggios with a light beat. swing: Easy swing: a laid-back tune, walking bass and a ride pattern.

key.description: Such as "D minor". Default: chosen from the style by the seed.

voices.description: Replace the sound of any part, for example {"lead": {"voice": "preset", "preset": "TripleOscillator/Square.xpf", "volume": 14}}.

tools.name: list_dj_effects
tools.description: List the DJ effects dj_effects can apply, with what each sounds like and its parameters.

tools.name: dj_effects
tools.description: Apply DJ effects to a rendered WAV at bar positions: filter_sweep, phaser, flanger, beat_repeat, gate, tape_stop, spinback, echo_out, scratch, reverse, noise_riser, pump and cut. Effects run in order, so a later one hears the earlier ones. Optionally masters the result to a loudness target. See list_dj_effects for parameters.

audio.description: Workspace WAV: a mix or one stem.

offsetSeconds.description: Where bar 0 starts in the file. 0 for anything rendered by this server.

targetLufs.description: Integrated loudness target in LUFS, for example -16 for game music.

ceilingDb.description: Peak ceiling in dBFS for the built-in limiter (default -1 when a loudness target is set).

tools.name: rearrange_audio
tools.description: Cut a rendered WAV into a new order by bar ranges, as a DJ edit: repeat a section, drop the intro, jump to the break. Segments are joined with short fades.

audio.description: Workspace WAV: a mix or one stem.

offsetSeconds.description: Where bar 0 starts in the file. 0 for anything rendered by this server.

targetLufs.description: Integrated loudness target in LUFS, for example -16 for game music.

ceilingDb.description: Peak ceiling in dBFS for the built-in limiter (default -1 when a loudness target is set).

tools.name: build_library_page
tools.description: Write one self-contained HTML page that shows the whole sound library with filters: the measured factory presets, stock LMMS samples, workspace samples, files in LMMS_SAMPLE_LIBRARIES and library phrases. Workspace renders tagged with tag_sound are listed as finished pieces with filters for composer, era, genre, mood, game use, arrangement and licence, their credits and their source note (<name>.source.md); untagged files are listed as before. Search, filter by type, source, role and tag, sort, click or use the arrow keys to listen, star picks and copy them as JSON. Samples play straight from disk; presets and phrases are listed with measurements and drawings but have no audio.

tools.name: build_library_previews
tools.description: Render a short audio clip for factory presets and library phrases so the library page can play them. Presets play a four-note figure; pitched phrases play over Am G F E with a plain synth, drum phrases with their own samples, progressions as held chords. Clips are trimmed, set to the same peak level and written to the library-previews folder. Work is done in batches: call again until remaining is 0, then rebuild the page with build_library_page.

limit.description: How many clips to render in this call.

redo.description: Render again even when a clip exists.

tools.name: find_loop_points
tools.description: Read-only. Find the tempo, beat grid and best loop regions of any audio file, including music made outside LMMS. Candidates are whole numbers of bars, scored by how closely the audio after the loop end matches the loop start and by spectrum and waveform on both sides of the seam. Says plainly when a person should pick.

audio.description: A workspace audio file: WAV at any common sample rate, or MP3, OGG or FLAC (these need ffmpeg). It may sit one folder down.

bpm.description: Tempo hint. Overrides detection; use it when you know the tempo or detection is unsure.

tools.name: prepare_loop
tools.description: Turn any audio file into game-ready loop files: a seamless loop (crossfaded or with the tail folded in), an optional separate intro one-shot, WAV and optionally OGG at the source sample rate, loudness and peak control, and a manifest like export_game_audio writes, plus the source file, tempo, confidence and seam score. Choose a candidate from find_loop_points, give startSeconds and endSeconds, or let it take the best candidate.

audio.description: A workspace audio file: WAV at any common sample rate, or MP3, OGG or FLAC (these need ffmpeg). It may sit one folder down.

name.description: Base file name. Default: from the source file name.

candidate.description: Rank from find_loop_points (run with the same bpm, beatsPerBar, minBars and maxBars).

bpm.description: Tempo hint. Overrides detection; use it when you know the tempo or detection is unsure.

intro.description: Write the audio before the loop as a separate one-shot intro.

seam.description: crossfade: fade at the seam, placed at a quiet point; linear when both sides are alike, equal-power when they are not. fold: add the audio after the loop end onto the loop start, for files that ring out.

targetLufs.description: Integrated loudness target in LUFS, for example -16 for game music.

ceilingDb.description: Peak ceiling in dBFS for the built-in limiter (default -1 when a loudness target is set).

ogg.description: Also write OGG Vorbis files (needs ffmpeg).

acceptLowConfidence.description: Use the best candidate even when find_loop_points says a person should pick.

tools.name: write_melody
tools.description: Write a phrase-based melody over a chord progression. One short idea is stated, answered, developed to a single climax and closed, with a rest after every phrase, chord tones on strong beats, velocities that swell and taper with each phrase, and optional grace notes. Returns a ready pattern of raw notes plus the motif and the phrase plan. Seeded: the same seed gives the same tune.

key.description: Tonic and mode, for example "D minor" or "Bb major".

chords.description: One entry per bar, looped to fill the piece. "Dm" fills a bar and "F C" splits it. A string may separate bars with |.

style.description: lyrical: singing lines. driving: busier, shorter notes. swing: triplet feel, laid back.

dynamics.description: How far velocities follow the phrase. 0 is flat.

ornament.description: Grace notes on the peak and a few long notes.

motif.description: Reuse a motif returned by an earlier call, so several parts or sections share one idea.

tools.name: write_accompaniment
tools.description: Write a backing part over the same chords: rolling arpeggios, broken chords or held blocks, voiced in the low register with the pedal held through each chord. Pass the plan from write_melody so it swells where the melody does.

chords.description: One entry per bar, looped to fill the piece. "Dm" fills a bar and "F C" splits it. A string may separate bars with |.

pedal.description: Let every note ring until the chord changes.

tools.name: import_midi
tools.description: Import a standard MIDI file from the workspace as an editable LMMS project: one piano-roll track per MIDI track (or merged into one), the time signature and tempo of the file, sustain pedal baked into note lengths and volume controller changes folded into velocities. form lays bars out in a new order, for example to unfold a repeat. Report the source tempo, metre and any changes it could not keep.

midi.description: A .mid file in the workspace, optionally one folder down.

bpm.description: Tempo for the project. Default: the first tempo in the file.

timing.description: score keeps the written rhythm at a steady tempo. seconds keeps the real timing of a recorded performance, including tempo changes, at the chosen tempo.

form.description: Bars to play, in order, numbered from 1 and inclusive. For a repeat with two endings, for example [{from:1,to:31},{from:32,to:39},{from:1,to:31},{from:40,to:47}].

tracks.description: MIDI tracks to import, by name or index. Default: every track with notes.

merge.description: Merge the chosen tracks into one track with this name, for example "Piano" so both hands play one instrument.

pedal.description: bake holds notes while the sustain pedal (CC64) is down, because LMMS patterns do not store controllers.

volumeChanges.description: fold scales note velocities by channel volume (CC7) and expression (CC11).

voice.description: Built-in voice for previews in LMMS. Use apply_preset to change it, or export_midi and render_vst3_stems for a sampled piano.

tools.name: master_audio
tools.description: Finish any workspace WAV, for example a render from render_vst3_stems: trim the silence after the last sound, fade the end, bring it to a loudness target under a true-peak ceiling and write WAV or OGG. Report loudness and peak before and after.

targetLufs.description: Integrated loudness target in LUFS, for example -16 for game music.

ceilingDb.description: Peak ceiling in dBFS for the built-in limiter (default -1 when a loudness target is set).

trimTail.description: Cut the end after the sound has fallen below -70 dBFS, keeping tailSeconds.

tools.name: develop_motif
tools.description: Develop one short motif instead of writing a new tune for every section. Takes a melody line (NOTE:steps, r:steps for rests) or raw notes plus a key, and returns diatonic variations as melody lines ready to paste into a pattern melody: repeat, sequence up or down, fit to a chord, inversion, retrograde, augmentation, diminution, a rhythm change that keeps the contour, first or last fragment, call and response, and cadence endings. Every result stays in the key.

motif.description: A melody line such as "D5:2 F5:2 A5:4 G5:2 F5:2 E5:4", or raw notes in ticks (48 per beat).

key.description: Tonic and mode, for example "D minor", "F# dorian", "Bb major", "C harmonic minor".

operations.description: Which variations to return. Default: all.

chord.description: Chord for fit_chord, such as "Gm" or "F" (default: the tonic chord). For cadence and half_cadence, the chord under the last note: the ending then lands on one of its tones.

step.description: Scale steps per sequence move. Default 1.

rhythm.description: Rhythm change style. Default: the first of dotted, swap, even that changes the motif.

tools.name: shape_performance
tools.description: Make machine-exact notes sound played: velocity rises and falls across each phrase, the top note of each chord is voiced above the rest, downbeats lean slightly, phrase ends slow down (ritardando) and the last bars slow more, notes can be held by a simulated sustain pedal, and velocities vary slightly with a fixed seed. Moves notes and clips in time, so the song gets a little longer. Works on every instrument track, or the tracks named. Keeps velocities at or under 100 (MIDI 127) by default. Writes a new project copy.

tracks.description: Tracks to shape. Default: every instrument track with notes. Tracks left out keep their notes but still move in time with the rest.

phrases.description: Phrase lengths in bars, in order, from the score. Bars after the listed phrases use phraseBars.

dynamics.description: How much velocity rises to each phrase peak and falls after it.

voicing.description: Extra weight on the top note of each chord, less on inner notes.

accent.description: Lean on the first beat of each bar.

humanize.description: Random velocity variation, as a fraction.

rubato.description: How much the last beats of each phrase slow down. 0.12 is 12% slower at the phrase end.

finalRitardando.description: How much the last bars of the piece slow down.

melodyLead.description: Ticks the rest of a chord sounds after its top note. One tick is 1/48 of a beat.

pedal.description: Simulated sustain pedal: hold notes until the next bar, half bar or beat, but stop at the next strike of the same pitch.

velocityScale.description: Overall touch. 0.8 plays every note 20% softer, which on a sampled piano also picks a softer, darker layer.

strict.description: Stop with an error, writing nothing, when an arrangement check reports an error.

tools.name: list_phrases
tools.description: List reusable phrases: chord progressions, piano montunos, stabs and arpeggios, bass lines, short hooks, and conga, clave, cowbell and house kit grooves. Pitched phrases follow whatever chords they are placed over, so each fits any key. Best rated first, then least used. Shows the listener's rating and how often each has been used.

instrument.description: Such as piano, bass, congas, kit, clave.

style.description: Such as latin, house, salsa, spanish, ballad.

query.description: Words to find in the id, name or description.

key.description: Show each progression as chords in this key.

tools.name: get_phrase

tools.name: create_from_phrases

progression.description: Chord symbols ("Am G F E"), Roman numerals ("i bVII bVI V") or a progression phrase id ("prog-andalusian").

sections.description: Sections in order. Each restarts the progression; give a section its own progression for contrast.

name.description: Track name for a pitched part. Parts with the same name share one track, so a piano can play a montuno in one section and stabs in another.

octave.description: Octave of the first chord root. Default 2 for bass, 4 for harmony, 5 for lead.

stretch.description: 2 plays the phrase at half speed (a one-bar sixteenth figure becomes two bars of eighths, as salsa is written).

gain.description: Scales the volume of every drum in a rhythm phrase.

variation.description: Random velocity movement so repeats are not identical.

sections.description: Section names this part plays in. Default: all.

sounds.description: Which sample plays each percussion sound, for example { "conga-open": { "sample": "latin-perc/Conga_HitN_v2_rr1_Sum.wav" } }. Unlisted sounds use the stock LMMS sample.

soundFolder.description: Workspace folder holding the percussion library files named in get_phrase (the CC0 VCSL set). Sounds found there are used instead of the stock stand-ins.

name.description: Track name for a pitched part. Parts with the same name share one track, so a piano can play a montuno in one section and stabs in another.

tools.description: Save a phrase to the listener's own library so it can be reused in any key. Either capture it from a project track (give the bars and the chords they were written over) or write it in phrase notation.

voices.description: Rhythm phrase: sound name to step grid.

tools.description: Record what the listener thought of a phrase, 1 (never again) to 5 (keep using it). list_phrases puts the best rated first. Pass rating null to clear it.

tools.description: Convert an SFZ instrument from LMMS_SAMPLE_LIBRARIES into a Decent Sampler .dspreset in the workspace, with absolute sample paths. sfz.description: Path of the .sfz file relative to LMMS_SAMPLE_LIBRARIES.

only.description: Keep only regions whose sample path contains this text, for example "alt_" or "/mid/".

tools.name: write_solo
tools.description: Write a solo line for one instrument over chords. Returns notes for a pattern, split into short and long notes so a staccato and a sustained sound can share the line, with a per-phrase summary and the scale used over each chord.

seed.description: Change it for a different solo over the same chords.

low.description: Lowest MIDI note. Trumpet 58, alto sax 55, flute 60.

tools.name: tag_sound
tools.description: Write or update the metadata sidecar (<name>.meta.json) for a workspace sound, render or project: title, composer, composed, era, genre, mood, gameUse, arrangement, instrumentation, durationSeconds, loop, source, licence, credits, date, kind, tags, notes and sourceNote. merge (default) keeps fields you do not pass and removes a field passed as null; replace writes only what you pass. composer.description: Composer as people search for them, for example "Erik Satie". Use "original" work's author for new music.

gameUse.description: Where in a game it fits.

arrangement.description: How this version treats the music: straight (as written), shaped (performed), or a restyle.

instrumentation.description: Instruments or sound sources, for example "Splendid Grand Piano".

durationSeconds.description: Filled in from the audio when left out.

loop.description: True when the file loops cleanly in a game.

source.description: Where the score, MIDI or recording came from.

licence.description: Use one spelling per licence: "public domain", "CC0", "CC-BY 3.0", "CC-BY 4.0", "CC-BY-SA 4.0", "MIT", "all rights reserved".

date.description: The day this file was made, YYYY-MM-DD.

kind.description: piece (finished music), sound (a sample or one-shot) or stem. A tagged file at the top of the workspace is a piece unless this says otherwise.

tags.description: Free tags; they join the tag filter on the library page.

sourceNote.description: A workspace .md file about where the music came from, when it is not next to the sound as <name>.source.md.

measure.description: Fill in durationSeconds from the audio when it is not set.

tools.name: list_tagged
tools.description: List workspace sounds and pieces by their metadata sidecars, filtered by any field: composer, era, genre, mood, gameUse, arrangement, licence, kind, loop, instrumentation, title or free text. Text fields match part of a value ("satie" finds "Erik Satie"); list filters match any value given. Each result gives its files, metadata and source note. targetLufs.description: Integrated loudness target in LUFS, for example -16 for game music.

tools.name: export_midi
tools.description: Export instrument patterns and arranged Beat/Bassline clips as multitrack MIDI at a static tempo.

instructions: LMMS MCP composes, edits, analyses and exports editable game audio using saved LMMS projects. Start with get_started for workflow and local capabilities, then use tools/list for exact schemas. For a musical brief, list_composer_profiles and create_composer_sketch or create_project. Search and audition sounds with search_sounds and preview_sound. Edit and mix with apply_edits. Render before delivery, inspect levels and the loop seam with analyze_audio, then use export_game_audio for loops, layers and stingers. Preserve the editable MMP or MMPZ and its referenced samples. A beat is 48 ticks and a 4/4 bar is 192 ticks. Project bars start at zero. Stock LMMS handles saved projects. Fathom rendering and Windows live control require optional local components. Use list_external_tools to discover optional VST3 instruments and related setup instructions. Arrangement rules: give every track a role (drums, bass, harmony, lead, counter, texture or fx). One lead melody at a time, with at most one counter-melody under it. Bass and harmony support the lead and stay out of its register. Build sections by repeating and varying one motif, and leave space.
